summary: Ten-lens review of the Composer Detail Level Wave 3 plan across three fix rounds. 120 original findings (9 BLOCKER / 37 MAJOR / 64 MINOR, plus 2 a11y non-severity rows and 8 leverage recommendations) were all dispositioned; the sign-off round returned 112 ACCEPT / 3 ACCEPT-PARK / 5 REJECT / 13 NEW across the ten reviewers, and every REJECT and NEW was applied in Rounds 2 and 3. Zero findings remain open. The final residual (Task 5 Step 6 had a commit message but no `git add`) was applied by the hub after architecture's Round-3 sign-off and is verified present in the reviewed artefact. Remaining items are three deliberate ACCEPT-PARK rulings, a set of execution cautions the reviewers recorded as non-defects, and two Roadmap tickets the leverage analyst asks be filed rather than built into this wave. One condition is load-bearing: leverage's N3 endorsement flips to REJECT if the producer cross-check pin is dropped or its no-dispatch sentence softened.

baseline.note: Three distinct commits, deliberately not collapsed. The plan's own Global Constraint (reality-A MAJOR-5) forbids writing any single sha as 'current': citations were verified at c601c957b; the fix rounds and all ten sign-offs ran at 7d0fdf534 (docs-only delta from c601c957b); this report was written at 28030f28c after a large tier-model burndown merge landed. See warning W13 for the one citation class that drifted.

recommendations.recommendation: The producer cross-check pin must survive execution intact. Task 3's ruling says 'without it this task should not be dispatched' — that sentence must not be softened, and the pin must not be dropped if it proves fiddly to write.
recommendations.rationale: The wave ends with two implementations of 'which fields publish a connection' either way it is planned (GraphView's `registerProducer` plus `graphTopology`'s `buildConnectionProducers`); `nodeTargets` never existed in the tree, so the improvement is not a reduced count but a change of character — from undiscoverable-and-untested to discoverable, unit-tested, and bound to the first by an agreement pin on one shared fan-in/fork fixture. Drop the pin and what remains is two rival topology implementations with nothing comparing them, which is the exact defect Task 3 exists to close, relocated rather than removed.
recommendations.consequence_if_ignored: leverage's N3 endorsement flips from ACCEPT to REJECT.

recommendations.recommendation: Honour the per-task `git add` discipline. Every task's `git add` must enumerate every path in its Files block; the standing rule at the top of Sequencing is now true of every task in the wave, including Task 5's nine per-step commits.
recommendations.rationale: Three separate staging gaps (Tasks 3, 9 and 10) came from `Commit.` with no pathspecs, and the class recurred once more at Task 5 Step 6 — the largest step in the task, whose commit MESSAGE got close scrutiny while its staging got none. Task 5 also holds the `AcknowledgementCard.tsx` collision with Task 1, so it is the wave's highest staging-risk surface.
recommendations.consequence_if_ignored: A commit that looks done and fails its own gate, or a broad `git add` that sweeps a sibling lane's work.

recommendations.recommendation: Task 3 Step 3 must run pytest, including `tests/unit/web/composer/test_producer_resolver.py`, before Step 4 commits.
recommendations.rationale: Task 3's relocation breaks three Python tests that hard-anchor `_GRAPH_VIEW_PATH`; the original evidence line claimed it could not. The frontend-only gate would have gone green on a change that reds the Python suite, and the parity module's own import is module-level, so a wrong symbol name fails at COLLECTION and errors all five tests at once.
recommendations.consequence_if_ignored: A green frontend gate certifying a red backend suite.

The cheap 80% is already taken inside Task 2 — the helper's header now states the usage convention ('Every component test that renders user-facing prose calls this helper'), which is the line that reaches someone who has never seen the file.

The ticket must also carry the explicit 'do NOT build a wrapper component / HOC' instruction with its three-way reason (RecoveryDiff; the blob preview; a refetch CADENCE, which is not visible content at all).

The `filigree create` invocation was also verified live and corrected (TITLE is positional, `-d/--description`; there is no `--title` and no `--body`), so the first draft of the command would not have run.

Its Round-1 NEW (Task 3's `git add` omitted files the fix round had added) generalised into a standing staging rule that caught two more gaps; its Round-2 NEW then found that rule overclaiming coverage on Task 5. Round 3 closed eight of nine Task 5 steps, and the hub applied the ninth (Step 6's two pathspecs), which this synthesis verified present.

quality.summary: Found that `modelDisplayName` strips the PROVIDER from run-confirm egress lines. It framed this as needing an operator ruling; the fix applied it rather than parking, because the plan's own Global Constraint already commits the wave. Its second BLOCKER — the shared gate helper extended with no self-test — produced Task 2's new `defaultDomPins.test.ts`. Its Round-1 NEW caught seven fixtures that would fail the plan's own `tsc` gate. Its Round-2 NEW found the prescribed `allowSelectors` remedy had no narrow implementation (the option removes whole elements, not substrings), fixed in Round 3 by an `egress-provider` product span. One ACCEPT-PARK: the mermaid hazard, bounded by measurement.

systems.summary: Converged with architecture on the Task 3 BLOCKER, and separately found Task 11 non-re-runnable with its lint baseline in `/tmp`. Its two REJECTs shared one cause and were the sharpest catch of the sign-off round: the new parity assertion imported `CoalesceSpec`, which does not exist (`core/config.py` declares `CoalesceSettings`) — and because the import is module-level, the wrong name fails at collection and errors all five tests, reddening Task 3's own gate for a reason unrelated to the relocation. Its NEW converged with reality-A on the hoist range.

signoff_r2.note: no REJECT or NEW rows filed, so no re-sign-off round was required

prior-art.summary: Its BLOCKER — `buildConnectionIndex`'s producers half re-derives GraphView's registry — is the finding that reshaped Task 3. The full lift it asked for was unavailable (`ProducerInfo` carries `edgeType`/`label` per registration, which a `Map<string, string[]>` cannot reconstruct), so the report's attached condition was met instead: the divergence is stated and both indexes are pinned against one shared coalesce fixture, with GraphView's `:1245-1351` registry hoisted into an exported `buildProducerRegistry(state)` to make it reachable. Task 4's private `nodeTargets` helper is deleted. Signed ACCEPT on the direct question: single authority for the rule Task 4 consumes.

tests.summary: Converged with quality on the untested gate helper and supplied the three-case structure. Its M1 (Task 9's pin passes vacuously) was applied while both of its specifics were rejected with evidence — it re-measured and upheld both rejections, recording that it had inferred flag names from tooltip prose instead of grepping the `flag:` keys, and that its own proposed remedy would have been vacuous. Its Round-1 NEW found a tautology in the guard test it had asked for. In Round 2 it withdrew its own earlier ACCEPT of M2's fix and confirmed the fourth mutation case is real.

a11y.summary: Its BLOCKER routed egress consent detail into `title` on a non-interactive `<li>`, unreachable by keyboard and by most screen readers; the fix uses `.sr-only` + `aria-describedby` per line, the pattern the file's own comment prescribes. Its most consequential NEW corrected an error three other parties had accepted: `closest()` checks the element itself and then walks up, so a tag qualifier narrows which elements MATCH a selector, never which elements an exemption REACHES — the whole Spec tab was still exempt and the plan's 'two exact elements' claim was false. The remedy adds a second option matched with `el.matches()` plus a fourth mutation case. Its ConfirmDialog sub-half is the one park.

leverage.summary: Two recommendations became Roadmap tickets rather than Wave 3 scope (R4, R5), and its four negatives — findings whose recommendation is 'change nothing' — were recorded as such rather than silently dropped. Its narrow REJECT caught a Roadmap row banking a mitigation Task 2 did not deliver; the fix made the claim true by adding the usage convention to the helper's header. IMPORTANT: its N3 endorsement is CONDITIONAL. The producer cross-check pin is the entire thing holding the two-implementation outcome together; if the pin is dropped or the 'without it this task should not be dispatched' sentence softened, N3 flips to REJECT. See recommendation R1.

process_notes: Ten independent lenses, three fix rounds, and a per-finding sign-off round in which each reviewer re-verified only its OWN findings by content (line numbers shifted every round) rather than re-reviewing the plan.
The fix pass ran read-only against the tree throughout: no git write commands, and only the one permitted file was edited.

Five claims were settled by EXECUTION rather than reasoning: the e2e TS7016 (confirmed by running tsc), the mermaid fence count (grep -c returns 0), the parity mechanism's feasibility against Pydantic `model_fields`, the two producer divergences, and the leaf-module import contract. The `filigree create` CLI flags were also re-verified live, catching a command in the plan that would not have run.
Round 3 was re-signed by only three of the ten lenses (reality-A, reality-C, architecture) — the other two Round-3 items were applied without re-verification by their authors. See warning W12.
The verdict is APPROVED_WITH_WARNINGS rather than APPROVED because three ACCEPT-PARK rulings and a set of execution cautions remain live, not because any finding is unresolved.
